citation: Herman, K. C., Reinke, W. M., Dong, N., & Bradshaw, C. P. (2022). Can effective classroom behavior management increase student achievement in middle school? Findings from a group randomized trial. Journal of Educational Psychology, 114(1), 144-160. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000641 (Advance online publication November 5, 2020.)
report_number: DOI 10.1037/edu0000641; IES-funded efficacy trial of the CHAMPS classroom management program (Missouri Prevention Science Institute, University of Missouri). IES award R305A130375 'Evaluation of a Classroom Management Training Program for Middle School Teachers'.
design: Group (cluster) randomized controlled trial; unit of randomization = Teacher/Class (teachers randomized to CHAMPS vs business-as-usual control within 9 urban middle schools, K=9 schools, randomization blocked within school). Subject: standardized academic achievement (state MAP English & math + SAT-10 reading comprehension & problem solving) plus social-behavioral outcomes. Grades 6-8 (middle school). Original sample 102 teachers / 1,450 students; final analytic samples vary by outcome (see effect rows). Comparison = business-as-usual (control teachers received no CHAMPS training; no alternative treatment). Two-level HLM (students nested in teachers), multiple imputation for missing data, controlling for prior-year pretest + demographics.
problems: (1) SOURCE = legal author/funder institutional repository copy hosted by the Missouri Prevention Science Institute (moprevention.org), the authors' own research center at the University of Missouri (not a piracy site, not ResearchGate/academia.edu). This is the accepted-manuscript version of the APA Journal of Educational Psychology article (DOI 10.1037/edu0000641); pagination differs from the published 114(1):144-160 version but all tables/numbers are present. (2) The paper reports model-based Cohen's d directly for each academic outcome but does NOT print the standardizing SD or the d-scale SE; the impact SE in Tables 6/7 is on the raw coefficient (b) scale. I derived g and its SE from the reported d and the b-scale SE: SE(d) = SE(b) * d/b (equivalently SE(d) = SE(b)/s where s = b/d is the implied standardizing SD). This reproduces the paper's reported p-values almost exactly (e.g., MAP English d/SE(d)=2.00 -> p~.046 vs reported .044; SAT-10 problem solving =1.97 -> p=.049 exact; SAT-10 reading =0.92 -> p=.36 exact), confirming the derivation is internally consistent. (3) The treatment/control split of n is not printed per academic outcome (Table 1 gives the social-behavioral baseline split of 637 control / 607 treatment, which is a DIFFERENT, larger analytic sample than the academic samples), so n_t/n_c are left null and the total per-outcome student N is recorded in notes; the cluster-adjusted HLM SE already accounts for the design so no central n-based variance recomputation is needed. (4) Hedges' J small-sample correction applied using df = total students - 2 (J ~ 0.9987-0.9988, negligible at these N). (5) n_clusters = number of teachers contributing to each academic outcome (47 for math-class outcomes, 54 for English/reading-class outcomes); icc = the design-effect (unconditional) ICC reported for each outcome in Tables 6/7. (6) NON-ACHIEVEMENT outcomes are NOT extracted (per spec): teacher-reported concentration problems (d=-.14, Table 3), disruptive behavior, emotional dysregulation, prosocial behavior (all null, Table 3), classwork completion (b=4.32, p=.008) & homework completion (Table 4), observed student time-on-task (d=0.16, Table 5), and all teacher-implementation outcomes (STOIC adherence d=0.62; BCIO-R positive-negative ratio d=0.39) -- these are behavior/SEL/teacher-practice measures, not student academic achievement. (7) Both achievement test batteries are standardized/independent (MAP = Missouri statewide standardized assessment; SAT-10 = published norm-referenced standardized achievement test), so all four extracted rows are include-eligible under central logic.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CHAMPS classroom management TPD (single treatment arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Missouri Assessment Program (MAP) Grade-Level Assessment - English/Language Arts subtest (state standardized test)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of year 1; spring MAP of the intervention school year)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d where d=0.14 is the model-based effect size reported by the authors (Table 6, p.11/published p.154) for the CHAMPS Intervention coefficient b=0.12 on MAP English, from a 2-level HLM controlling for prior-year MAP English pretest + demographics (students nested in teachers). J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) = 0.99883 (df = 646-2). g_se = J*SE(d), SE(d) = SE(b)*d/b = 0.06*0.14/0.12 = 0.07 (implied standardizing SD s = b/d = 0.857); g_var = g_se^2. Check: d/SE(d)=2.00 ~ reported p=.044.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 6 (MAP Academic Outcomes), manuscript p.11 (published 114(1):154); abstract & Main Effects on Student Academic Outcomes section
effect_sizes.notes: Significant positive achievement effect: b=0.12, SE=0.06, p=.044, d=0.14. State standardized ELA test -> Reading. Analytic sample = 54 teachers, 646 students (English/reading classes); per-arm n split not reported. Conditional ICC=0.031, unconditional (design) ICC=0.304 (Table 6). Pretest-adjusted (prior-year MAP English) and cluster-adjusted (2-level HLM). This MAP English result is the abstract's headline academic finding alongside SAT-10 problem solving.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CHAMPS classroom management TPD (single treatment arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Stanford Achievement Test 10th Edition (SAT-10) - Reading Comprehension subtest (publisher standardized test)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (April/May of the intervention school year)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d where d=0.08 is the model-based effect size reported by the authors (Table 7, p.11/published p.154) for the CHAMPS Intervention coefficient b=3.04 on SAT-10 Reading Comprehension, from a 2-level HLM controlling for SAT-10 reading pretest + demographics. J = 0.99881 (df = 632-2). g_se = J*SE(d), SE(d) = SE(b)*d/b = 3.31*0.08/3.04 = 0.0871 (implied s = b/d = 38.0); g_var = g_se^2. Check: d/SE(d)=0.918 ~ reported p=.359 (non-significant).
effect_sizes.notes: Non-significant positive achievement effect: b=3.04, SE=3.31, p=.359, d=0.08. SAT-10 reading comprehension subtest (administered to students in reading/English classes) -> Reading. Analytic sample = 54 teachers, 632 students; per-arm n split not reported. Conditional ICC=0.052, unconditional (design) ICC=0.271 (Table 7). Pretest- and cluster-adjusted. Note: b is on the SAT-10 scaled-score scale (intercept ~694), hence large b for a small d.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CHAMPS classroom management TPD (single treatment arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Missouri Assessment Program (MAP) Grade-Level Assessment - Mathematics subtest (state standardized test)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of year 1; spring MAP of the intervention school year)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d where d=0.16 is the model-based effect size reported by the authors (Table 6, p.11/published p.154) for the CHAMPS Intervention coefficient b=0.15 on MAP math, from a 2-level HLM controlling for prior-year MAP math pretest + demographics. J = 0.99873 (df = 594-2). g_se = J*SE(d), SE(d) = SE(b)*d/b = 0.10*0.16/0.15 = 0.1067 (implied s = b/d = 0.9375); g_var = g_se^2. Check: d/SE(d)=1.50 ~ reported p=.105 (non-significant).
effect_sizes.notes: Non-significant positive achievement effect: b=0.15, SE=0.10, p=.105, d=0.16. State standardized math test -> STEM. Analytic sample = 47 teachers, 594 students (math classes); per-arm n split not reported. Conditional ICC=0.196, unconditional (design) ICC=0.231 (Table 6). Pretest- and cluster-adjusted.

effect_sizes.arm_label: CHAMPS classroom management TPD (single treatment arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Stanford Achievement Test 10th Edition (SAT-10) - Problem Solving (mathematics) subtest (publisher standardized test)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (April/May of the intervention school year)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d where d=0.17 is the model-based effect size reported by the authors (Table 7, p.11/published p.154) for the CHAMPS Intervention coefficient b=5.66 on SAT-10 Problem Solving, from a 2-level HLM controlling for SAT-10 problem-solving pretest + demographics. J = 0.99872 (df = 587-2). g_se = J*SE(d), SE(d) = SE(b)*d/b = 2.87*0.17/5.66 = 0.0862 (implied s = b/d = 33.29); g_var = g_se^2. Check: d/SE(d)=1.97 ~ reported p=.049 (significant).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 7 (SAT-10 Academic Outcomes), manuscript p.11 (published 114(1):154); abstract
effect_sizes.notes: Significant positive achievement effect: b=5.66, SE=2.87, p=.049, d=0.17. SAT-10 math problem-solving subtest (administered to students in math classes) -> STEM. Analytic sample = 47 teachers, 587 students; per-arm n split not reported. Conditional ICC=0.049, unconditional (design) ICC=0.155 (Table 7). Pretest- and cluster-adjusted. This is the abstract's headline math finding (b is on SAT-10 scaled-score scale, intercept ~641).
